rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person reference to first-person plural signals special divine concern for the matter.
rows.anchor: والالتفات فيها من الغيبة إلى التكلم مع الغير للإشارة إلى كمال العناية بأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After showing God's creation and governance of the heavens, earth, and their contents, the verse challenges polytheists to show any creation by their alleged gods.
rows.anchor: لما رأهم خلقه وتدبيره تعالى للسماوات والأرض وما عليها فأثبت به ربوبيته وألوهيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge establishes God's sole divinity and lordship: if the idols cannot create anything, they cannot be gods or lords.
rows.anchor: فإن لم يقدروا على إرادة شيء ثبت بذلك وحدانيته تعالى في الوهيته وربوبيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though polytheists assign governance, not creation, to idols, creation and governance are inseparable; a real governor would create what it governs.
rows.anchor: لأنه نسب إلى الله خلقا هو بعينه تدبير من غير انفكاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative challenge is spoken by the Prophet, since this form of address cannot properly come from anyone else.
rows.anchor: وقد سيقت الآية خطابا من النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لأن نوع هذا الخطاب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi reports that 31:6 concerned al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who bought Persian stories and told Quraysh them to divert listeners from the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: فيستمعون حديثه ويتركون استماع القرآن. عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i notes that al-Bayhaqi's report from Ibn Abbas gives the same account.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا المعنى في الدر المنثور عن البيهقي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this account may have occasioned revelation of the entire sūrah.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يكون ذلك سبب نزول تمام السورة كما تقدمت الإشارة إليه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام والرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Abdillah says lahw al-hadith includes singing; al-Kafi transmits the same gloss from him and from al-Rida.
rows.anchor: في المعاني بإسناده عن يحيى بن عبادة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قلت قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Muslim reports Abu Ja'far saying singing is among deeds for which God threatens the Fire, and he recites 31:6.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول الغنا مما أوعد الله عليه النار

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Basir reports Abu Ja'far's ruling: earnings from singing women visited by men are forbidden, while women invited to weddings are permissible; he cites 31:6.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال سألت أبا جعفر عليه السلام عن كسب المغنيات فقال التي يدخل عليها الرجال حرام

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Umama attributes to the Prophet a prohibition on teaching or selling singing women and taking their price; the next segment supplies the report's wording.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع وروى أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The narration prohibits teaching or selling singing women and taking their price; al-Durr al-Manthur says many compilers report it from Abu Umama and the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ورواه في الدر المنثور عن جم غفير من أصحاب الجوامع عن أبي أمامة عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Abdillah explains lahw al-hadith as attacking and ridiculing truth, recalling Abu Jahl's mock offer of dates and butter as the promised zaqqum; it also includes singing.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام أنه قال هو الطعن في الحق والاستهزاء به

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: A report from Ali ibn al-Husayn says a nation containing the barbat, a stringed instrument, is not sanctified.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي الدنيا عن علي بن الحسين قال ما قدست أمة فيها البربط

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu al-Jarud reports Abu Ja'far identifying the person in 31:6 as al-Nadr, who knew people's stories and poetry; the account continues into 31:7.
rows.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Rida says the heavens are joined to earth like interwoven fingers: supporting pillars exist, but cannot be seen, reconciling the image with 13:2.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه عن الحسين بن خالد عن أبي الحسن الرضا عليه السلام قال قلت له أخبرني عن قول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever submits to God and acts righteously while certain of the Return will ultimately be saved, since their end is with God, who promises success.
rows.anchor: ومن وحد الله وعمل صالحا مع اليقين بالمعاد فهو ناج غير هالك البتة في عاقبة أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return of all outcomes to God explains the command to grasp the firmest handle, a representational metaphor for salvation and success.
rows.anchor: بما أنه استعارة تمثيلية عن النجاة والفلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage consoles the Prophet against grief over disbelief: the disbelievers return to God, who discloses the reality and consequences of their deeds, namely the Fire.
rows.anchor: تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وتطييب لنفسه أن لا يغلبه الحزن وهم بالآخرة راجعون إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brief worldly enjoyment followed by forced punishment clarifies that disbelievers never leave God's governance; they remain overpowered by him in every state.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أنهم غير خارجين من التدبير قط وإنما يمتعهم في الدنيا قليلا ثم يضطرهم إلى عذاب غليظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists are disposed toward monotheism: asked who created heaven and earth, they acknowledge God without recognizing the implications.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنهم مفطورون على التوحيد معترفون به من حيث لا يشعرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since governance cannot be separated from creation, acknowledging God as Creator entails that he governs, gives and withholds, and alone is the hoped-for and feared deity.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان الخالق هو هو فالمدبر لها هو هو لأن التدبير لا ينفك عن الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to praise God for the polytheists' unwitting admission; most fail to understand that it entails God's exclusive lordship and divinity.
rows.anchor: أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يحمد الله على اعترافهم من حيث لا يشعرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A few understand the implication but refuse the truth and deny what they inwardly know, as in the account of Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: نعم قليل منهم يعلمون ذلك ولكنهم لا يطاوعون الحق بل يجحدونه وقد أيقنوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership proves exclusive lordship and divinity; creation completes the prior argument because it necessarily entails governance and disposal.
rows.anchor: وكان نفس الخلق كافيا في استلزامه اكتفى به في تمام الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As source of creation and giver of every perfection, God must possess all that beings need; otherwise he could not originate or give it, so he is absolutely independent.
rows.anchor: فهو واجد لكل ما يحتاج إليه الأشياء فهو غني على الإطلاق إذ لو لم يكن غنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absolute independence entails that God owns everything and may dispose of it freely; no other entity can independently own or govern creation.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان غنيا على الإطلاق كان له ما في السماوات والأرض فهو المالك لكل شيء على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd is praise for chosen beauty; because every beauty in the world is God's, praise returns to him and he is absolutely praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: أن الحمد هو الثناء على الجميل الاختياري وكل جميل في العالم فهو له سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If any beautiful, ordered governance came from another independently, praise would belong to that other, contradicting God's absolute praiseworthiness.
rows.anchor: لكان الحمد والثناء لغيره تعالى لا له فلا يكون حميدا على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min shajaratin explains the preceding relative expression; the singular collective tree, in the conditional construction, means every tree on earth.
rows.anchor: من شجرة } بيان للموصول والشجرة واحد الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-baḥr means the sea in general; seven seas means seven additional equivalents, with seven denoting abundance rather than an exact count.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالبحر مطلق البحر، وقوله {

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The number seven is used for abundance rather than to specify exactly seven added seas.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالسبعة التكثير دون خصوص هذا العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A word is an expression indicating meaning; in divine usage God's words can designate existents brought forth by his command and Jesus as God's word.
rows.anchor: والكلمة هي اللفظ الدال على معنى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If every tree became a pen and the sea plus seven equivalents became ink for God's words, the ink would run out first because his words are limitless.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى ولو جعل أشجار الأرض أقلاما وأخذ البحر وأضيف إليه سبعة أمثاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is elliptical; the closing attributes explain that no one can overpower God and that in his wisdom he does not delegate governance.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن في الكلام إيجازا بالحذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is unassailable and wise, so writing cannot exhaust what comes from him and he does not entrust governance to another.
rows.anchor: حكيم لا يفوض التدبير إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the proof of God's exclusive governance, this verse illustrates the vast reach of his creative and governing commands.
rows.anchor: والآية متصلة بما قبلها من حيث دلالته على كون تدبير الخلق له سبحانه لا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The death angel's taking of souls answers the deniers' question about being lost in the earth and resolves their objection; treating tawaffī as generic death misses the wording's point.
rows.anchor: وظهر بما تقدم أولا وجه اتصال قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is among the clearest Qur'anic proofs that the soul is immaterial, distinct from the body and its states.
rows.anchor: أن الآية من أوضح الآيات القرآنية الدالة على تجرد النفس بمعنى كونها غير البدن أو شيء من حالات البدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nukūs al-ra's means lowering or bowing the head.
rows.anchor: نكس الرأس إطراقه وطأطأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals specifically are deniers of resurrection, identified by the verse's conclusion and the definite article's anaphoric reference to them.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالمجرمين بقرينة ذيل الآية خصوص المنكرين للمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their standing before their Lord echoes the earlier statement that they denied meeting him; now they face the encounter they could not admit.
rows.anchor: { عند ربهم } محاذاة لما تقدم من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they saw by direct vision and heard through obedience, now recognizing that salvation requires faith and righteous action.
rows.anchor: أبصرنا بالمشاهدة وسمعنا بالطاعة فارجعنا نعمل عملا صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the encounter, shame and regret make deniers acknowledge what they rejected and beg to return: they have certainty but lack righteous deeds, and will not return.
rows.anchor: وقد حصل لهم الإيمان اليقيني وبقي العمل الصالح ولذا يعترفون باليقين ويسألون الرجوع إلى الدنيا

words: وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَءَاتَيْنَا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ هُدَىٰهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could guide every soul by willing that each person, including a disbeliever, choose guidance; compulsion would invalidate moral responsibility and reward.
rows.anchor: بأن نشاء من طريق اختيار الكافر وإرادته أن يتلبس بالهدى فيتلبس بها من طريق الاختيار والإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fixed decree to fill Hell with jinn and humans came when Iblis refused to bow to Adam and vowed to mislead all except God's sincere servants.
rows.anchor: وهو إملاء جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين وهو قوله لإبليس لما امتنع من سجدة آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is a distinctive cognitive assent of the soul whose consequence is practical commitment; fisq is departure from that commitment and from servitude.
rows.anchor: الإيمان سكون علمي خاص من النفس بالشيء ولازمه الالتزام العملي بما آمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq's root is illustrated by a date slipping out of its skin; its broader sense is leaving the bounds of servitude.
rows.anchor: من فسقت التمرة إذا خرجت عن قشرها ومآل معناه الخروج عن زي العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a rhetorical denial of equality, reinforced by the explicit statement that the two groups are not equal.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام في الآية للانكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ma'wā is a place where a person takes refuge and settles.
rows.anchor: المأوى المكان الذي يأوي إليه ويسكن فيه الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuzul means food and drink prepared for a guest, then was generalized, as some say, to any gift.
rows.anchor: والنزل بضمتين كل ما يعد للنازل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell as their abode implies permanence, reinforced by their being returned whenever they try to leave.
rows.anchor: كون النار مأواهم لازمه خلودهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who transgressed are deniers of Resurrection; their address in Hell repays their mockery of believers' belief in it during worldly life.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن المراد بالذين فسقوا هم منكرو المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the hoped-for return is repentance, the nearer punishment is worldly warning, such as famine, illness, or killing; the greater is punishment on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: مثل السنين والأمراض والقتل ونحو ذلك قبل العذاب الأكبر يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says al-adnā suits warning better than al-aṣghar, which makes punishment sound lesser, or al-ab'ad, which does not fit the threatening context.
rows.anchor: لأن المقام مقام الإنذار والتخويف

words: ذُكِّرَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ ثُمَّ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away after reminders from God's signs explains the greater punishment: it is the gravest injustice.
rows.anchor: فعلله بأنهم ظالمون أشد الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause explains punishment of the unjust: they are criminals, and their punishment is God's retribution against criminals.
rows.anchor: والعذاب انتقام منهم، والله منتقم من المجرمين

words: فَلَا تَكُن فِى مِرْيَةٍ مِّن لِّقَآئِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book given to Moses is the Torah, and al-mirya means doubt or skepticism.
rows.anchor: المراد بالكتاب التوراة والمرية الشك والريب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view makes the pronoun refer to Moses, the object of meeting: the Prophet met him during the Night Journey, either as reminder if the sūrah came later or promise if earlier.
rows.anchor: فقيل الضمير لموسى وهو مفعول اللقاء والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah was guidance to its followers and nurtured people God selected for Imamate, who guided by his command; it was blessed in practice and afterward.
rows.anchor: أنها هدى في نفسه يهدي من اتبعه إلى الحق

words: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement is religious, driven by mutual injustice and envy; God will settle it on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: يريد اختلافهم في الدين وإنما كان ذلك بغيا بينهم

words: فَلَا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَّآ أُخْفِىَ لَهُم
rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Sa'd reports that the Prophet described Paradise as containing what no eye has seen, ear heard, or heart imagined, then recited 32:16–17; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
rows.anchor: من طريق أبي صخر عن أبي حازم عن سهل بن سعد قال

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Majma' reports Abu Abdillah saying every good deed has a stated Qur'anic reward except night prayer, whose reward God left unstated for its great worth.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام أنه قال ما من حسنة إلا ولها ثواب مبين في القرآن إلا صلاة الليل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi transmits the same teaching from Abu Abdillah through his father, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and Asim ibn Humayd: night prayer's immense reward is unspecified.
rows.anchor: حدثني أبي عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي نجران عن عاصم بن حميد عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The same report says God honors believers each Friday: an angel brings two garments and escorts them toward the gathering in Paradise.
rows.anchor: إن الله عز وجل كرامة في عباده المؤمنين في كل يوم جمعة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: At the Friday gathering God reveals himself—explained by the narrator as his mercy—and says there is no prostration or worship; he grants believers seventy times what they possess in Paradise.
rows.anchor: فإذا اجتمعوا تجلى لهم الرب تبارك وتعالى فإذا نظروا إليه أي إلى رحمته

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Believers return every Friday with seventyfold what they had; the report identifies this increase with 50:35 and urges remembrance and praise on Friday.
rows.anchor: فيرجع المؤمن في كل جمعة بسبعين ضعفا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The narration says believers' wives find them newly radiant and that God made a garden unseen by creatures, renewing its fragrance each morning, linked to 32:17.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى خلق جنة بيده ولم يرها عين ولم يطلع عليها مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the end of the Friday-garden narration explains its beginning; “meaning his mercy” is the narrator's gloss.
rows.anchor: أقول ذيل الرواية تفسير لصدرها

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah reports Abu Abdillah saying only God knows the Hereafter reward for feeding a believer until satisfied, not even an angel or prophet.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن ميمون القداح عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من أطعم مؤمنا حتى يشبعه

words: أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِنًا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقًا
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu al-Jarud reports Abu Ja'far's account that Ali and al-Walid ibn Uqba argued; after al-Walid boasted of his eloquence, spear, and battlefield stance, Ali called him a transgressor and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i notes this occasion report in al-Majma' from al-Wahidi and Ibn Abbas, and in al-Durr al-Manthur through multiple transmitters and authorities.
rows.anchor: ورواه في المجمع عن الواحدي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a disputation before Muawiya, al-Hasan tells al-Walid that Ali flogged him eighty lashes for wine and killed his father at Badr, while God calls Ali a believer and al-Walid a transgressor.
rows.anchor: في الاحتجاج عن الحسن بن علي عليه السلام في حديث يحاج فيه رجالا عند معاوية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Idris al-Khawlani reports that the Prophet identified the nearer punishment as worldly disasters, illnesses, and hardships for transgressors, but purification and expiation for believers.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إدريس الخولاني قال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
rows.claim: Al-Majma' reports from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah that the nearer punishment is the Beast and the Dajjal.
rows.anchor: في الرواية عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليه السلام أن العذاب الأدنى الدابة والدجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about a word its speaker will say is from 23:100; God's word is truth and his guidance leads to good and happiness, so people should follow him rather than their own claims.
rows.anchor: كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God reports something, reality matches it; when he establishes a ruling, its effects follow and it matches the real benefit.
rows.anchor: إن أخبر عن شيء كان الواقع مطابقا لما أخبر به وإن أنشأ حكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām indicates specification: calling adopted children to their fathers means attributing them to those fathers.
rows.anchor: للاختصاص أي ادعوهم وهم مخصوصون بآبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in huwa aqsaṭ refers to the verbal noun implied by “call them,” as in 5:8; aqsaṭ is comparative from qisṭ, justice.
rows.anchor: صيغة تفضيل من القسط بمعنى العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing them to their fathers is the more just course before God.
rows.anchor: لأن الدعاء لآبائهم أعدل عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not knowing their fathers means not knowing their identities; do not invent lineage, but address them as brothers and allies in religion.
rows.anchor: المراد بعدم علمهم آباءهم عدم معرفتهم بأعيانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawālī here means allies or guardians.
rows.anchor: عدم معرفتهم بأعيانهم، والموالي هم الأولياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no sin for mistaken attribution through lapse or forgetfulness, but deliberate false attribution is sinful; God's forgiveness here concerns the mistake.
rows.anchor: أي لا ذنب لكم في الذي أخطأتم به لسهو أو نسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet has greater claim than believers in protection, care, love, honor, accepting his call, and fulfilling his will, in worldly and religious affairs.
rows.anchor: فالمحصل أن ما يراه المؤمن لنفسه من الحفظ والكلاءة والمحبة والكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet faces danger, believers should shield him at their own cost, love and honor him above themselves, and obey him over personal wishes.
rows.anchor: فليقه المؤمن بنفسه ويفده نفسه وليكن النبي أحب إليه من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the narrower view that the Prophet's priority applies only when he summons believers against their inclination; the unrestricted wording gives him broader priority.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر ضعف ما قيل إن المراد أنه أولى بهم في الدعوة
